<reason>Both sides were sharp, but PRO controlled the decisive clash. CON's strongest moves were the "such as" scope argument (Big Five swept in) and the gut-feel counterfactual. PRO neutralized the scope point cleanly in A1 by reading the motion's "because" clause as scoping its target, and then turned CON's own pressure answer ("keep using them... letter as a headline you can ignore") into the case: the letter is the product employers actually use, the workshop is named after it, so CON is defending a different instrument inside MBTI/DISC packaging. CON's "stop using vs. drop the codes" distinction remained a live route, and the contestable-score-vs-gut-feel point was never fully closed by PRO, but PRO's "bias with a score attached" and the convenience-confession flip of [A2.8] did real damage. CON also had two clipped speeches, an execution cost. PRO's asymmetry weighing (conversation available anyway vs. sticky, flippable label) gave the cleaner reason to vote.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's A1 in Rebuttal 2 ([B4.1]-[B4.2]): answering CON's Big Five trap by arguing the motion's stated reason scopes its target, then exposing that CON needs conscientiousness "inside the tent" because DISC has no predictive muscle of its own — followed by seizing CON's "ignore the letter" concession as the motion with a face-saving clause.</best_rebuttal>
